expectations.text: Identifies the Article 38 opt-out covering Articles 21, 22 and 33(2)
expectations.evidence: Never cites Article 38 or the actual deferred provisions (Arts. 21, 22, 33(2)); instead names DPO appointment and transfer assessments as the deferred items

expectations.text: States the opt-out runs five years
expectations.evidence: States the relief 'I believe 5 years from the effective date (to about 1 January 2031)' and repeats 'the relief is, as I recall, 5 years'

expectations.text: Notes micro-enterprises and household businesses are exempt from the same provisions
expectations.evidence: 'Micro enterprises, small enterprises and startups (and household businesses) get a transitional period' - same relief extended to them

expectations.text: Makes clear other PDPL duties still apply
expectations.evidence: 'Core obligations are not deferred: lawful basis and consent, notice, data subject rights, security measures, breach notification...'

expectations.text: Does not cite invented chapter numbers
expectations.evidence: Cites no chapter numbers at all, so none invented
